To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the first inhibitors of the δ-CAs that have been shown to be effective against this enzyme class.
we have investigated the inhibition of the δ-CAs TweCAδ from Thalassiosia weissflogi using a panel of thiocarbamate compounds and identified some of the most effective inhibitors to date.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new series of potent and selective inhibitors for TweCAδ, a marine enzyme belonging to the δ-CA class.
the discovery of new molecular probes for investigating the role that δ-CAs play in the carbon fixation process in diatoms.
the identification and characterization of new inhibitors of δ-carbonic acid anhydrase (TweCAδ) from the diatoms Thalassiosria weissflogi.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the δ-CAs from diatoms and other algae are not inhibited by the majority of the compounds that are active against mammalian and pathogen CAs, and that the most potent inhibitors of TweCAδ are the mono-thiocarbamate of 3,4-DMPO (67.7 µM), and R-nipecotic acid di- thiocarbamate (93.6 µM).
TweCAδ is not significantly inhibited by any of the tested thiocarbamate compounds, but it was effectively inhibited by some piperazine derivatives.
TweCAδ is not significantly affected by the majority of the thiocarbamates investigated in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TweCAδ is not inhibited by most of the mono and di-thio carbamate compounds that were used in this study, but some of these inhibitors can be used as molecular probes to study this enzyme.

TweCAδ is not significantly inhibited by the majority of the mono- and di-carbamates tested, with the exception of some aliphatic and aromatic derivatives, and some compounds incorporating the R-enantiomers of the piperazine moiety.
TweCAδ was inhibited with a KI in the micromolar range by most of the mono- and di-carbamic compounds tested.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the δ-class CAs are less prone than α- and β-CAs to inhibition by the mono and di-thio-carbamates.
